subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is classified as a hardwood?
questions.explain: Hardwoods come from deciduous (broadleaved) trees such as oak, while pine, spruce and cedar are softwoods from coniferous trees.

questions.q: What defining feature does a ferrous metal contain?
questions.explain: Ferrous metals contain iron, which makes most of them magnetic and prone to rusting.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a thermoplastic?
options: It can be reheated and reshaped many times
It sets permanently and cannot be remoulded
It contains iron and is magnetic
It is a naturally occurring timber
questions.explain: Thermoplastics such as acrylic and HDPE soften on heating and can be reshaped repeatedly, making them recyclable.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy made mainly from which two metals?
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, whereas bronze is copper and tin.

options: Two or more materials combined to gain enhanced properties
A polymer that changes colour with heat
A timber taken from a coniferous tree
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials so the result has better properties than either material alone, e.g. GRP.

questions.q: Which smart material changes colour in response to a change in temperature?
questions.explain: Thermochromic pigments change colour with temperature; photochromic materials respond to light instead.

questions.q: Hardness is best defined as a material's resistance to which of the following?
questions.explain: Hardness is the ability to resist wear, abrasion, scratching and indentation.

questions.q: Why can a thermosetting plastic not be remoulded once it has set?
options: It melts at too low a temperature
It undergoes a permanent chemical change (cross-linking) when heated
It is a naturally occurring material
It contains iron which hardens on cooling
questions.explain: Thermosetting plastics form permanent cross-links when first heated and cured, so they cannot be softened and reshaped again.

questions.q: A material described as ductile can best be:
options: Drawn out into a thin wire
Compressed into thin sheet without cracking
Stretched and then snap back to shape
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to be stretched (in tension) and drawn into wire without breaking; copper is a good example.

questions.q: Glass reinforced plastic (GRP) is made by combining which components?
options: Carbon fibres in an epoxy matrix
Glass fibres in a polyester resin matrix
Wood particles in a glue binder
questions.explain: GRP consists of glass fibres embedded in a cured polyester resin, giving a strong, lightweight composite.

questions.q: How does a shape memory alloy such as Nitinol behave?
options: It conducts more electricity as it is compressed
It returns to a pre-set shape when heated
It glows when a voltage is applied
It changes colour in bright sunlight
questions.explain: A shape memory alloy can be deformed but returns to its original 'remembered' shape when heated above a set temperature.

questions.q: Malleability is the property that allows a material to be:
options: Drawn into a wire under tension
Deformed by compression (e.g. hammering or rolling) without cracking
Returned to shape after a load is removed
Melted and cast into a mould
questions.explain: Malleability is the ability to be shaped by compressive forces such as hammering or rolling without fracturing.

questions.q: A tough material is one that can:
options: Absorb impact and shock without fracturing
questions.explain: Toughness is the ability to absorb energy from impacts without breaking, the opposite of brittleness.

questions.q: MDF, plywood and chipboard are all examples of:
questions.explain: These are manufactured (man-made) boards produced from wood fibres, veneers or particles bonded together.

questions.q: A designer needs a material for a lightweight, transparent, recyclable fizzy-drinks bottle. Which is most suitable?
questions.explain: PET is a lightweight, transparent, tough thermoplastic that is widely recycled, making it ideal for drinks bottles.

questions.q: A mug is designed to reveal a hidden picture only when a hot drink is poured in. Which smart material achieves this?
questions.explain: Thermochromic pigments change colour with temperature, so the design appears when the mug heats up.

questions.q: Window frames for a coastal house must be lightweight and highly resistant to corrosion. Which metal is the best choice?
questions.explain: Aluminium is a lightweight non-ferrous metal that forms a protective oxide layer, giving excellent corrosion resistance.

questions.q: A suspension spring must return to its original shape after each load is removed. Which property is essential?
questions.explain: Elasticity is the ability of a material to return to its original shape once a deforming force is removed, as required in a spring.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Material Classification
